\chapter{Winning and prizes}

\hlchaptermodality{547}

\begin{chapteropening}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 547: I can talk about a win, a championship, a trophy and a medal, and say that a team qualified.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{فوز} (fawz)}{فوز (fawz)}]{\ar{فوز} (fawz) — a triumph; a win}

\label{lesson:AR-C547-fawz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to pass the ball, then the Arabic for to compete.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{فوز}}
\textbf{\ar{فوز}} — \emph{fawz} — \textquotedblleft{}a triumph; a win\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{احتفل} \ar{اللاعبون} \ar{بالفوز}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{iḥtafala al-lāʿibūn bi-l-fawz.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The players celebrated the win.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{فوز}} (\emph{fawz}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-w-z}, \textquotedblleft{}to win, to escape safely\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Fāza, to win, which you know, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fawz}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fawz}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iḥtafala al-lāʿibūn bi-l-fawz.} — The players celebrated the win.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to pass the ball, then the Arabic for to compete, then say \emph{fawz} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{فوز} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A triumph; a win\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{بطولة} (buṭūla)}{بطولة (buṭūla)}]{\ar{بطولة} (buṭūla) — a championship; heroism}

\label{lesson:AR-C547-butula}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to compete, then the Arabic for a triumph.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{بطولة}}
\textbf{\ar{بطولة}} — \emph{buṭūla} — \textquotedblleft{}a championship; heroism\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{فاز} \ar{فريق} \ar{المدرسة} \ar{بالبطولة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{fāza farīq al-madrasa bi-l-buṭūla.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The school team won the championship.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{بطولة}} (\emph{buṭūla}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{b-ṭ-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to be void, to be idle; to be brave\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives the root both senses: baṭāla is idleness, and baṭal a brave man.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{buṭūla}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{buṭūla}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fāza farīq al-madrasa bi-l-buṭūla.} — The school team won the championship.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to compete, then the Arabic for a triumph, then say \emph{buṭūla} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{بطولة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A championship; heroism\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{كأس} (kaʾs)}{كأس (kaʾs)}]{\ar{كأس} (kaʾs) — a trophy; a cup}

\label{lesson:AR-C547-kas}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a triumph, then the Arabic for a championship.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{كأس}}
\textbf{\ar{كأس}} — \emph{kaʾs} — \textquotedblleft{}a trophy; a cup\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{رفع} \ar{الفريق} \ar{الكأس} \ar{بعد} \ar{المباراة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rafaʿa al-farīq al-kaʾs baʿda al-mubārā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The team lifted the trophy after the match.
\end{quote}

It is also a drinking glass.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{كأس}} (\emph{kaʾs}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{k-ʾ-s}, \textquotedblleft{}a cup, a drinking vessel\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives kaʾs as a cup with drink in it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaʾs}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaʾs}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rafaʿa al-farīq al-kaʾs baʿda al-mubārā.} — The team lifted the trophy after the match.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a triumph, then the Arabic for a championship, then say \emph{kaʾs} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{كأس} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A trophy; a cup\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ميدالية} (mīdāliya)}{ميدالية (mīdāliya)}]{\ar{ميدالية} (mīdāliya) — a medal}

\label{lesson:AR-C547-midaliya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a championship, then the Arabic for a trophy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ميدالية}}
\textbf{\ar{ميدالية}} — \emph{mīdāliya} — \textquotedblleft{}a medal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{فاز} \ar{أخي} \ar{بميدالية} \ar{ذهبية}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{fāza akhī bi-mīdāliya dhahabiyya.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother won a gold medal.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ميدالية}} (\emph{mīdāliya}) is a modern loan, usually traced to Italian \emph{medaglia} or French \emph{médaille}, which go back to Latin \emph{metallum}, \textquotedblleft{}metal\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mīdāliya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mīdāliya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fāza akhī bi-mīdāliya dhahabiyya.} — My brother won a gold medal.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a championship, then the Arabic for a trophy, then say \emph{mīdāliya} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تأهل} (taʾahhala)}{تأهل (taʾahhala)}]{\ar{تأهل} (taʾahhala) — to qualify}

\label{lesson:AR-C547-taahhala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a trophy, then the Arabic for a medal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تأهل}}
\textbf{\ar{تأهل}} — \emph{taʾahhala} — \textquotedblleft{}to qualify\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تأهل} \ar{فريقنا} \ar{إلى} \ar{البطولة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taʾahhala farīqunā ilā al-buṭūla.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our team qualified for the championship.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتأهل}, \emph{yataʾahhal}.

It takes \ar{إلى} or \ar{لـ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تأهل}} (\emph{taʾahhala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʾ-h-l}, \textquotedblleft{}a family; to be fit for\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Form V taʾahhala is to become fit for a thing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʾahhala}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʾahhala}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʾahhala farīqunā ilā al-buṭūla.} — Our team qualified for the championship.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a trophy, then the Arabic for a medal, then say \emph{taʾahhala} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تأهل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To qualify\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
